notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.41_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.41.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.41.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Fixed

- **Messages you send from a phone now actually leave it.** A conversation is
  two documents, one written by each of you, and yours was only ever introduced
  to the devices belonging to *your* account. Your friend's copy was introduced
  to one device of theirs: whichever machine happened to be in front of you the
  day you became friends. So a friendship made at a desktop and then carried on
  from a phone left the phone and your friend with no way to find each other,
  and everything typed on the phone stayed on the phone — while their messages
  still arrived, because their half of the conversation was introduced properly.
  That is exactly the "I can read but not reply" this has been doing, and why it
  came back to life whenever the desktop was switched on to bridge the two. Both
  halves now start from everything the app knows: your devices, their devices,
  and whoever is actually connected at the time.

- **Calls between friends carry sound.** Ringing worked, answering worked, both
  screens said a call was in progress, and no audio or video connection was ever
  opened. A call connects to the devices it has been told are there, and for a
  conversation that list was empty and always had been — nothing was recording
  who was on the other end of a conversation's documents. The app now dials
  whoever is saying out loud that they are in the room, which is something
  everybody in a call broadcasts anyway, so both ends find each other whichever
  one arrives first.

- **Joining a call already in progress connects you to everybody in it.** In a
  server this used to reach only the handful of people the app happened to be
  exchanging updates with at that moment, so in a busy room some pairs simply
  never heard each other. Anybody who arrives later, and anybody the first
  attempt could not reach, is now picked up within a few seconds.

- **Sending a message to a friend no longer waits for the network.** Pressing
  send cleared the box and disabled the button while the app opened both halves
  of the conversation and joined a group — seconds on a phone with a day of
  catching up to do, which read as a send that did nothing. The message is
  written and drawn immediately, exactly as in a server channel, and shows a
  retry if it fails. Opening a conversation shows what is on the device first
  too, rather than after the same wait.

- **Picking your phone up after a while catches it back up.** Android freezes an
  app the moment it stops being visible, so a phone that went into a pocket on
  Wi-Fi and came out on cellular has had every connection quietly invalidated
  with nothing running to notice. Coming back to the app now rejoins your
  conversations, says where you are again, and re-reads the conversation on
  screen, your friends list and any call in progress.

- **Messages arriving in a conversation nobody is watching are no longer held
  back.** When a friend appeared to go offline the app tried to close the
  conversation down, which stopped it announcing new messages without actually
  stopping them arriving — so they landed silently and only appeared when the
  conversation was closed and opened again. Conversations now stay open.

- **Being on two devices no longer makes you flicker.** Your phone and your
  desktop each say where they are, and each was overwriting the other's answer.
  Sitting in a call on a phone meant dropping out of the room in everybody
  else's list every time the desktop said hello. Both are now heard separately.

- **Friends read as offline less often.** Whether somebody was there was decided
  by one signal that is only ever a partial view, so a perfectly reachable
  friend could show as away — with the call buttons greyed out to match. Three
  signals answer it now, and any of them is enough.

- **Direct messages show whether they have been delivered.** The mark that says
  a message has not reached anyone yet was switched off for conversations,
  because nothing was reporting when one had. Something does now.

- **Moving between live channels tells the room you left.** You went on showing
  as present in the old one for over a minute.

- **The connection page can see your friends.** It only ever drew servers, so
  somebody who uses Ruze to talk to one friend and is in no servers opened it to
  a picture of nothing at all while everything worked.
